raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so every bag I buy matters. I will still follow the same wheat-maize way I have used for years, because on small land I cannot gamble. I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little by looking at water, fertilizer price, and what the better growers around me are doing. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put most of the phosphorus in first, then split the nitrogen so the wheat stands strong through winter and greens up well in spring. I have well water, so I will not let the wheat go thirsty at overwintering, jointing, and filling if the ground is dry. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people here do, because the yield is steadier. After wheat harvest I will move fast, keep the stubble, and do light or no tillage so I do not lose moisture and I can save labor. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield costs more, so I will feed both crops a bit on the safe side. I will spray when I see real pressure, but I will not skip the main disease and insect timings.
